title: Show the real ratcheted trailing/profit-protecting stop, not just the raw protective stop, in the Portfolio positions list and Stock Detail page
description:
User-requested gap: `GET /api/portfolio/risk`'s `RiskPosition.trailing_stop` (`app.portfolio.risk.ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`, Elder ch. 54 'Don't Let a Winning Trade Turn into a Loss') is computed by the backend for every open position, but confirmed via grep this session that NO frontend component currently reads `trailing_stop`/`trailingStop` -- only `frontend/src/api/types.ts` (the generated type definitions) even mentions the field. Every place the UI shows a stop today reads only the raw, un-ratcheted `protective_stop`: `PositionsTable.tsx`'s 'Protective Stop' column (~line 186, the Portfolio page's positions list -- the 'tickers list' in the user's own phrasing), `RiskPanel.tsx`'s `protective_stop` column (~line 102), and `HeldPositionBanner.tsx`'s 'Current Stop' field (~line 157, the Stock Detail page -- the 'ticker details' in the user's own phrasing).

Why this matters, read directly from `risk.py`'s own docstrings: `trailing_stop` is a hard ratchet -- per `GET /api/portfolio/risk`'s own documented guarantee, it can never be lower than any value already reported for that position before, even if today's raw price-action formula would suggest a lower number (ch. 54's 'move your stop only in the direction of your trade' rule). `protective_stop` has no such guarantee; it's a pure point-in-time recomputation that CAN go down. Before the breakeven-profit trigger first fires, `trailing_stop` simply equals `protective_stop` (read `ratchet_trailing_profit_stop`'s docstring, risk.py ~line 290 onward) -- the two numbers only diverge once a position has earned enough unrealized profit (10% of entry price) for the ratchet to start protecting it. So a user watching only `protective_stop` today is seeing a number that can visibly drop even though the real, governing stop the backend has already computed never did -- and for a position that HAS earned that profit, they're simply not shown the higher, more protective number at all.

This is a genuine design decision, not a mechanical add-a-field change: because the two values coincide most of the time (before the ratchet first triggers), showing both as two permanently-separate, usually-identical columns would be redundant most of the time for most positions. Decide and record (don't silently pick without justifying) whether to: (a) promote `trailing_stop` to be the primary 'stop' figure shown in the existing column/field (since it's the one that's actually governing and never loosens -- closer to what a trader should trust), with the raw `protective_stop` demoted to a secondary detail (e.g. inside the existing `MetricHelp` popover, or a small inline note only when the two values actually differ), or (b) add a wholly separate, always-visible second column/field for `trailing_stop` alongside the existing `protective_stop` one in both locations. Check whether an existing `MetricHelp` entry already explains the protective-stop-vs-trailing-stop distinction (`metricHelpContent.ts` in both `features/portfolio/` and `features/stocks/`) before writing a new one.

checklist.step: Read `risk.py`'s `trailing_profit_stop`/`ratchet_trailing_profit_stop` docstrings in full, and `RiskPosition.trailing_stop`'s own schema description in schemas.py, to confirm the exact current semantics before changing any UI (source may have shifted since this task was written).

Decide and record (as a `decisions` entry) how `trailing_stop` is surfaced relative to the existing `protective_stop` display in both locations -- promoted-primary-value-with-raw-as-detail vs. a separate adjacent column/field -- and why.

Add or extend `MetricHelp` content explaining the protective-stop-vs-trailing-stop distinction if not already adequately covered by an existing entry, consistent with this app's existing `metricHelpContent.ts` conventions.

Tests for both changed components confirming `trailing_stop` is actually read and rendered (not just that the component still renders at all), covering both the pre-ratchet (trailing_stop == protective_stop) and post-ratchet (trailing_stop > protective_stop) cases.

decisions.decision: Promoted `RiskPosition.trailing_stop` to be the primary 'Stop' value shown in all three existing locations (`PositionsTable.tsx`'s and `RiskPanel.tsx`'s stop column, renamed from 'Protective Stop' to 'Stop', and `HeldPositionBanner.tsx`'s field, renamed from 'Current Stop' to 'Stop'), with the raw, un-ratcheted `protective_stop` demoted to a new `MetricHelp` popover (`stopHelp` in `features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts`) attached to each of those three values. The popover's `interpretValue` always states both figures and explicitly says whether they currently differ (and in which direction, tighter/higher or looser/lower) rather than silently going quiet once they diverge.
decisions.rationale: Rejected the alternative (a second, always-visible, permanently-separate column/field for trailing_stop alongside protective_stop) because the two values are identical for the common case (before a position's unrealized profit crosses the 10%-of-entry-price breakeven-ratchet trigger) -- a second column would mostly show a duplicate of the first for most positions most of the time, adding table width/field clutter for little information gain. Promoting trailing_stop as primary instead shows the number that's actually governing/never loosens (closer to what a trader should trust per Elder ch. 54's 'move your stop only in the direction of your trade'), while the raw, more-volatile protective_stop figure stays one click away via the existing MetricHelp affordance this app already uses for comparable detail (e.g. PositionProfitTargetCell's profit-target breakdown) -- no information is dropped, just reprioritized. Checked both `features/portfolio/components/metricHelpContent.ts` and `features/stocks/components/metricHelpContent.ts` for an existing protective-stop-vs-trailing-stop MetricHelp entry before writing `stopHelp`; neither had one. Renamed the column header/field label from 'Protective Stop'/'Current Stop' to the generic 'Stop' in all three locations (rather than keeping the old label while silently swapping the underlying value) since the label should describe what's actually displayed now, not what used to be displayed; RiskPanel's own `protective_stop` column was given the identical treatment even though the task's checklist named only PositionsTable.tsx explicitly, since both are portfolio-risk tables showing the exact same field and leaving one updated and one not would have reintroduced the same inconsistency this task exists to fix.

review.notes: Full review: backend pytest (1618 passed, 99.94% cov) and frontend vitest (1051 passed, 99.77%+ cov) both green with no regression; ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc/profit-target-wording-guard all clean; code-review skill (high effort) found zero correctness findings; validate_tasks.py clean. Read the diff line-by-line in all three components (PositionsTable.tsx, RiskPanel.tsx, HeldPositionBanner.tsx) and confirmed trailing_stop (not protective_stop) is what's rendered, with protective_stop always passed through to stopHelp.interpretValue so it's never dropped -- verified via grep that no stale 'Protective Stop'/'Current Stop' label references were left behind anywhere in frontend/. Read (not just trusted) the pre-ratchet and post-ratchet test cases in all three *.test.tsx files plus metricHelpContent.test.ts's direct stopHelp.interpretValue unit tests -- both directions (tighter/higher and looser/lower) and the equal case are genuinely asserted against the displayed value, not just rendered-at-all checks. Independently ran a live browser walkthrough against a freshly-started backend (FINTRADE_DATA_PROVIDER_MODE=fixture) + frontend: added a real AAPL position with ~72% unrealized profit (well past the 10%-of-entry ratchet trigger), confirmed GET /api/portfolio/risk returned a genuinely diverging protective_stop=269.56/trailing_stop=192.95, and screenshotted PositionsTable, RiskPanel, and HeldPositionBanner all showing $192.95 (the ratcheted figure) with the Stop-help popover correctly stating the looser/lower direction and both numbers. No console errors or failed/4xx+ network requests. Could not coax this fixture dataset's four low-noise steadily-trending series into the tighter/higher divergence direction live (needs a pullback-from-a-prior-peak shape they don't have at a scale that beats the 1/3-profit-fraction formula), but that direction is thoroughly covered by the genuine unit tests cited above. Also ran the e2e-test skill (make e2e): all 28 tests across all 6 spec files passed, no regression from the Stop rename/promotion. RiskPanel.tsx's scope extension beyond the task's literal checklist (promoting trailing_stop there too) is correctly scoped -- checked RiskPanel.test.tsx has no sort-specific tests that would conflict with the protective_stop->trailing_stop sort-key change, and the key change itself is actually a correctness improvement (DataTable's generic row[key] sort now sorts by the value actually displayed). The 'Stop' label (vs. keeping 'Protective Stop'/'Current Stop') is a reasonable UX tradeoff given the task's own recorded decisions entry and this app's existing MetricHelp-for-detail convention -- not blocking either way. No backend/API changes in this diff, so openapi.json regeneration doesn't apply. No non-blocking findings to track as a follow-up this round.

pr_decision.notes: Independently re-ran backend pytest (1618 passed, 99.94% cov) and frontend vitest (1051 passed, 99.77% stmt/99.05% branch cov) -- both match pr-reviewer's reported numbers exactly, no staleness. Re-ran ruff/mypy/eslint/tsc (all clean) and scripts/validate_tasks.py (clean). Skimmed the full diff myself in all three components plus metricHelpContent.ts/RiskPanel.tsx; confirmed DataTable sorts generically by row[sortKey] (frontend/src/components/common/DataTable/DataTable.tsx:109) so the protective_stop->trailing_stop sort-key change has no other dependents -- grepped for 'protective_stop' across frontend/src and found only test fixtures, doc comments, and openapi-derived types.ts descriptions, nothing live keyed off the old string. Did my own independent live-browser spot-check (not pr-reviewer's): started a fresh fixture-mode backend + Vite dev server, added a real AAPL position (cost basis $40 vs ~$275 current price, well past the 10%-of-entry ratchet trigger) via the API, and confirmed via a scripted Playwright session that PositionsTable, RiskPanel, and HeldPositionBanner all render $116.95 (trailing_stop) rather than the raw $269.56 (protective_stop), with the Stop-help popover correctly stating 'looser (lower) than today's raw protective stop (269.56)' and no console errors. Accept holds.
